prep-07-c1.quote: One of the 72 authors, Christopher Chambers, is a member of the Advisory Board of Nature Human Behaviour.

prep-07-c1.text: Daniel J. Benjamin, James O. Berger, Magnus Johannesson, et al (2018). Redefine statistical significance. Nature Human Behaviour.
prep-07-c1.quote: We propose to change the default P-value threshold for statistical significance from 0.05 to 0.005 for claims of new discoveries.
prep-07-c1.claim: to change the default p-value threshold for statistical significance from 0.05 to 0.005 for claims of new discoveries

prep-07-c1.text: Daniël Lakens, Federico G. Adolfi, Casper J. Albers, et al (2018). Justify your alpha. Nature Human Behaviour.
prep-07-c1.quote: In response to recommendations to redefine statistical significance to P ≤ 0.005, we propose that researchers should transparently report and justify all choices they make when designing a study, including the alpha level.
prep-07-c1.claim: they proposed that researchers should transparently report and justify all choices they make when designing a study, including the alpha level

prep-07-c1.text: American Statistical Association (2016). American Statistical Association Releases Statement on Statistical Significance and P-Values.
prep-07-c1.quote: In light of misuses of and misconceptions concerning p-values, the statement notes that statisticians often supplement or even replace p-values with other approaches.
prep-07-c1.claim: statisticians often supplement or even replace p-values with approaches that emphasise estimation over testing

prep-07-c2.text: John Protzko, Jon Krosnick, Leif Nelson, Brian A. Nosek, et al (2023). RETRACTED ARTICLE: High replicability of newly discovered social-behavioural findings is achievable. Nature Human Behaviour.
prep-07-c2.quote: When one lab attempted to replicate an effect discovered by another lab, the effect size in the replications was 97% that in the original study.
prep-07-c2.claim: Replications succeeded 86% of the time, and effects replicated at 97% of their original size.

prep-07-c2.text: John Protzko, Jon Krosnick, Leif Nelson, Brian A. Nosek, et al (2024). Retraction Note: High replicability of newly discovered social-behavioural findings is achievable. Nature Human Behaviour.
prep-07-c2.quote: The concerns relate to lack of transparency and misstatement of the hypotheses and predictions the reported meta-study was designed to test; lack of preregistration for measures and analyses supporting the titular claim
prep-07-c2.claim: lack of preregistration for measures and analyses supporting the titular claim

prep-07-c2.text: John Protzko, Jon Krosnick, Leif Nelson, Brian A. Nosek, et al (2024). Retraction Note: High replicability of newly discovered social-behavioural findings is achievable. Nature Human Behaviour.
prep-07-c2.quote: All authors agree to this retraction due to incorrect statements of preregistration for the meta-study as a whole but disagree with other concerns listed in this note.
prep-07-c2.claim: All authors agreed to the retraction because of incorrect statements of preregistration, but disagreed with the other concerns.

prep-07-c3.text: Andrew H. Tyner, Anna Lou Abatayo, Mason Daley, et al (2026). Investigating the replicability of the social and behavioural sciences. Nature.
prep-07-c3.quote: Here we attempted replications of 274 claims of positive results from 164 quantitative papers published from 2009 to 2018 in 54 journals in the social and behavioural sciences.
prep-07-c3.claim: Its replication study attempted 274 claims of positive results from 164 quantitative papers published from 2009 to 2018 in 54 journals across the social and behavioural sciences

prep-07-c3.text: Andrew H. Tyner, Anna Lou Abatayo, Mason Daley, et al (2026). Investigating the replicability of the social and behavioural sciences. Nature.
prep-07-c3.quote: Replications showed statistically significant results in the original pattern for 151 of 274 claims (55.1% (95% confidence interval (CI) 49.2–60.9%)) and for 80.8 of 164 papers (49.3% (95% CI 43.8–54.7%)), weighed for replicating multiple claims per paper.
prep-07-c3.claim: 151 of 274 claims (55.1%) replicated with significant results in the original pattern

prep-07-c3.text: Center for Open Science (2026). SCORE. Center for Open Science.
prep-07-c3.quote: Reproducibility tended to be higher in political science and economics, in more recent publications, and in journals that required data sharing.
prep-07-c3.claim: Reproducibility was higher in more recent publications and in journals that required data sharing, a hint that reforms pay off.
